problem: "A syllabus may call this async state initialisation because the first value is fixed when the component mounts" is not a standard term and is self-contradictory: nothing asynchronous happens, and the sentence does not name the real feature (passing a function to useState so an expensive initial value is computed only once). A student will memorise a wrong label.
fix: Replace with: "Initial value can be computed lazily: useState(() => buildRows()) calls buildRows only on the first render, not on every render. Some syllabi call this lazy initial state."

problem: The code prints direct = 1 using the single line direct = start + 1, so it never shows the three direct setCount calls being queued. The code is also plain Python in a React chapter, so a student may think it is the counter's real code.
fix: Either add three separate assignments (queued = start + 1 three times, keeping queued at 1) or keep the Python but add a comment that it models the queue, not the React source.

problem: PropTypes is described only as a "runtime check"; it is checked in development builds only and is stripped from production builds, so students may expect warnings in a deployed app.
fix: "PropTypes is a development-only runtime check: Greeting.propTypes = { name: PropTypes.string }. It warns in the console during development and is removed from production builds."

problem: "A hook is a React function whose name starts with use" states a naming convention as the definition; the name does not make a function a hook, it is a rule so React tooling can check hook rules.
fix: "A hook is a function that lets a component use React features; built-in hooks start with use, and custom hooks must follow that naming convention."
